{{context|date=January 2025}}
{{Short description|Purported social preference phenomenon}}
{{orphan|date=March 2024}}
The '''blue–seven phenomenon''' is a [[social phenomenon]] in which a purported statistical majority of people in the US choose the color [[blue]] and number [[7|seven]] when asked to [[randomly]] select a color and a single digit number. The cause of the [[cognitive bias]] is not understood,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Benel |first1=Russell A. |title=The "Blue–Seven Phenomenon" or the "Blue, Seven, … Phenomena"? |journal=The Journal of General Psychology |date=January 1976 |volume=94 |issue=1 |pages=145–146 |doi=10.1080/00221309.1976.9711600}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Saito |first1=Miho |title="Blue and Seven Phenomena" among Japanese Students |journal=Perceptual and Motor Skills |date=October 1999 |volume=89 |issue=2 |pages=532–536 |doi=10.2466/pms.1999.89.2.532|pmid=10597589 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Richard C Boutwell |author2=Patrice Fennell |title=Investigation and theoretical consideration of the "blue–seven" phenomenon |journal=The Journal of General Psychology |date=Oct 1, 1974 |volume=91 |pages=301–302}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Simon |first1=William E. |title=Number and Color Responses of Some College Students: Preliminary Evidence for a "Blue Seven Phenomenon" |journal=Perceptual and Motor Skills |date=October 1971 |volume=33 |issue=2 |pages=373–374 |doi=10.2466/pms.1971.33.2.373}}</ref> though it has been posited that both colors and numbers are imbued with layers of significance.<ref name="Christenfeld1995">{{cite journal |last1=Christenfeld |first1=Nicholas |title=Choices from Identical Options |journal=Psychological Science |date=Jan 1995 |volume=6 |issue=1|pages=50–55 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-9280.1995.tb00304.x |jstor=40062876}}</ref>

The existence of the phenomenon has been disputed.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Trueman |first1=John |title=Existence and Robustness of the Blue and Seven Phenomena |journal=The Journal of General Psychology |date=July 1979 |volume=101 |issue=1 |pages=23–26 |doi=10.1080/00221309.1979.9920057}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Knowles |first1=Philip L. |title=The "Blue Seven" is Not a Phenomenon |journal=Perceptual and Motor Skills |date=October 1977 |volume=45 |issue=2 |pages=648–650 |doi=10.2466/pms.1977.45.2.648}}</ref> Outside of the US, these preferences may not hold.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wiegersma |first1=Sjoerd |last2=Van Der Elst |first2=Gerard |title="Blue Phenomenon": Spontaneity or Preference? |journal=Perceptual and Motor Skills |date=February 1988 |volume=66 |issue=1 |pages=308–310 |doi=10.2466/pms.1988.66.1.308}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Letzter |first1=Rafi |title=Billions of people have the same favorite color and number, and scientists don't know why |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/blue-seven-phenomenon-2016-8 |work=Business Insider |date=Aug 12, 2016}}</ref> In other countries, differences occur, particularly in Northern Ireland where a noted bias of green and eight results in a ''green–eight'' phenomenon.{{Citation needed|date=May 2024}}
